headlines.title: 원·달러환율 17년만에 1500원 찍었다
headlines.summary: 1501원 출발 뒤 다소 하락세 국제유가 100달러 안팎 불안 석유최고가 1회 위반도 ‘아웃’ 미국이 이란 원유 수출 기지인 하르그섬의 군사시설을 공습하면서 국제 유가가 급등세를 보인 가운데 원·달러 환율이 17년 만에 주간거래에서 장중 1500원을 돌파했다.

headlines.summary: ■ 17년 만에 ‘1500원 터치’ 안전자산 달러 선호심리 극대화 “고유가 지속시 1500원선 고착” 민주, 이달내 추경안 국회 제출 16일 오전 서울 중구 하나은행 본점 딜링룸에서 관계자가 1500원을 넘어선 원·달러 환율을 불안하게 응시하고 있다. 원·달러 환율은 1501.0원으로 출발했다.

headlines.title: IEA 긴급비축유 방출 개시 … 韓, 시기·방식 저울질
headlines.summary: 정부, 2246만 배럴 방출 준비 “아시아·오세아니아 즉각 풀어” 미국·이란 전쟁으로 호르무즈 해협 봉쇄 위기 등 중동 사태가 악화일로에 접어들자 국제에너지기구(IEA) 회원국들이 긴급 비축유 방출을 개시하고 있다. 국내에서도 비축유 방출 방식과 시기별 방출량 등을 검토하며 방출 준비를 본격화하고 있는 것으로 알려졌다.

headlines.title: 환율 1500원 돌파 개장 … 금융위기 이후 처음

headlines.title: ‘ 6000피 ’ 재안착, 국제유가에 달렸다
headlines.summary: WTI 상승과 동시에 증시 약세 코스피와 단기 상관계수 -1 근접 “중동사태發 인플레 여부 촉각 반도체 등 기술기업 실적 주식” 중동발 지정학적 리스크로 국제유가가 급등락을 반복하면서 유가와 주가가 거의 완전한 ‘역상관 관계’를 보인다는 분석이 나왔다.

headlines.title: 정부, 이달말 추경안 국회제출 … 최대 20조 관측
headlines.summary: 유류비 지원 등 민생안정 대책 검토 피해 따른 선별지원, 지역화폐 거론 “법인세 등 초과세수 대부분 추경 투입” 중동 정세 악화로 국제유가가 요동치자 정부가 경기 하방 압력에 대응하기 위해 이달 말 추가경정예산(추경) 정부안의 국회 제출을 목표로 사실상 비상체제에 돌입했다.

headlines.title: 인천공항·한국공항공사 등 3곳 통폐합 검토 … 공공기관 개혁 ' 속도'
headlines.summary: 기능 유사 기관 통합해 공항 운영 효율성 제고 가덕도 재원 조달 목적 관측도…재경부 "결정된 바 없어" 인천국제공항 계류장에 항공기가 이륙하는 모습. 2026.3.15 ⓒ 뉴스1 이호윤 기자 (세종=뉴스1) 전민 기자 = 정부가 인천국제공항공사, 한국공항공사, 가덕도신공항건설공단 등 공항 관련 3개 공공기관의 통폐합 방안을 검토하고 있다.

headlines.title: 한경협 “ 고용 의 71 %는 서비스업 … 지원법 마련 시급”
headlines.summary: 총 부가가치의 61% 비중 차지 정부차원 생산성 향상 지원필요 국민소득 4만 달러 도약을 위해선 고용의 70% 이상을 차지하고, 부가가치의 60%를 넘어서는 국내 서비스산업을 체계적으로 지원하는 법·제도 마련이 시급하다는 제언이 나왔다. 한국경제인협회(한경협)는 국회와 정부에 서비스산업발전기본법의 조속한 제정을 촉구하는 의견서를 제출했다고 16일 밝혔다.

headlines.title: 서울 ‘ 구축 ’ 아파트 상승률 ‘ 신축 ’ 앞질렀다

key_headlines.title: Depleting Reserves and Securing Additional Crude Oil… Full Mobilization of Energy Stabilization Measures [US-Iran War]
key_headlines.summary: The government is fully mobilizing measures, including releasing reserves and securing more oil, to stabilize energy amidst the US-Iran conflict. The crisis management level for the Middle East situation has been elevated, and coal power plant generation limits are being lifted.

key_headlines.title: Won-Dollar Exchange Rate Hits 1500 Won for the First Time in 17 Years
key_headlines.summary: The Won-Dollar exchange rate briefly surpassed 1500 Won in intra-day trading for the first time in 17 years, starting at 1501 Won before slightly falling. This surge is attributed to the sharp rise in international oil prices following a US airstrike on an Iranian oil export facility.

key_headlines.title: Won-Dollar Exchange Rate Starts at 1501 Won Amid 'Oil Price Shock' – Third Wave Since FX/Financial Crisis
key_headlines.summary: The Won-Dollar exchange rate started at 1501 Won, marking its first touch of 1500 Won in 17 years and the third significant wave since past financial crises, driven by an oil price shock. The persistent high oil prices are expected to solidify the 1500 Won level.

key_headlines.title: IEA Begins Releasing Emergency Oil Reserves; South Korea Weighs Timing and Method
key_headlines.summary: IEA member countries have begun releasing emergency oil reserves in response to the escalating Middle East situation, including the potential blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. South Korea is preparing to release 22.46 million barrels and is actively reviewing the methods and timing for its own reserve release.

key_headlines.title: Exchange Rate Opens Above 1500 Won for the First Time Since Financial Crisis
key_headlines.summary: The Won-Dollar exchange rate opened at 1501.0 Won, surpassing 1500 Won for the first time since the 2009 financial crisis, primarily due to the US-Iran conflict. Amidst this volatility, 3-year Treasury bond yields reached a 21-month high, prompting the government and ruling party to consider bond buybacks if necessary.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Korean economy is grappling with significant turbulence due to the US-Iran conflict, pushing the Won-Dollar exchange rate above 1500 Won for the first time in 17 years, sparking fears of an "oil price shock." In response, the government has elevated its crisis management level for the Middle East situation and is preparing to release emergency oil reserves, while also lifting restrictions on coal power generation to ensure energy stability. High oil prices are also driving up import prices and causing complex calculations for central banks regarding interest rate adjustments.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Global central banks face complex decisions on interest rates, caught between rising inflation due to high oil prices and the burden on households if rates increase. South Korea's import prices have risen for an eighth consecutive month in February, climbing 1.1% from the previous month, marking the longest streak since 2008. Analysts predict a steeper rise in March, as recent US-Iran conflict impacts on global oil prices were not fully reflected in February's data, potentially pushing South Korea's growth rate to 0% if the crisis prolongs for a year.
sections.Financial Markets: Amid fluctuating oil prices and exchange rates driven by Middle East tensions, the KOSPI started strong, led by semiconductor stocks, but later saw mixed performance. Despite initial gains and positive influence from individuals and institutions, foreign investors net-sold significant amounts. US markets reacted positively to falling oil prices, with the Nasdaq rising, while bond yields declined. The volatility is expected to continue, influenced by the US-Iran conflict and upcoming FOMC decisions.
sections.Industry & Technology: Despite overall market volatility, certain sectors like semiconductors and defense/aerospace are seeing strong individual stock performance and new highs. SKC announced voluntary redundancies for employees hired before 2025 due to prolonged industry stagnation in batteries and petrochemicals, aiming to improve cost structure and organizational efficiency. Meanwhile, advancements in battery technology are highlighted, with Pil Energy showcasing its expertise at InterBattery and collaborating with Factorial on solid-state battery commercialization, alongside developments in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2X) technology.
sections.Real Estate: Amid soaring housing prices, "land-lease apartments," where residents only own the building but not the land, are gaining significant popularity, as evidenced by a 67.9:1 subscription rate in Magok. However, the rise in Seoul apartment prices has recently slowed, especially after presidential announcements regarding multi-homeowner capital gains tax, with the average selling price reaching 1.31 billion won. Additionally, many newly offered apartments this year have higher prices than surrounding market rates, leading some young people to cancel their housing subscriptions.
sections.International Economy: New York stock markets closed higher, driven by a drop in international oil prices, despite ongoing volatility from the Iran conflict. Global central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, are contemplating their interest rate decisions in a "super week" for rates, with the Fed widely expected to freeze its rates. Meanwhile, US President Trump is pressuring allies like South Korea and Japan, which are heavily reliant on oil transiting the Strait of Hormuz and host US military bases, to participate in the Strait's escort operations, after European countries declined.
sections.AI & Economy: The South Korean government, through the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, is actively promoting growth and re-leap for small business owners by fostering local entrepreneurs and expanding digital education, including AI. Shinsegae Group is partnering with Reflection AI, a US firm, to build the largest AI data center in South Korea, marking the first collaboration under the US government's AI export program. This initiative, aiming for 'Sovereign AI Factory,' is expected to boost local economies and establish a domestic AI infrastructure hub. Furthermore, AI drug development is attracting significant investment, with global pharmaceutical companies betting 130 trillion won on joint R&D.
sections.Others: Global pharmaceutical companies are increasingly investing in AI for joint R&D, with a staggering 130 trillion won being committed. The global cosmetics ODM market is seeing a shift in leadership from Europe to South Korea, indicating the rising dominance of K-beauty. In a broader economic context, SamilPwC predicts that AI-centric mega-deals will drive the M&A market in 2026. Separately, the South Korean presidential office stated it is in close contact with the US regarding Trump's request for South Korea to dispatch warships to the Strait of Hormuz, emphasizing a cautious approach.
